title: Mamie Smith's background and the Black Swan label with Alberta Hunter
summary: Spikes had traveled with Mamie Smith in Bill Bailey's show; Alberta Hunter made the first recording of Someday Sweetheart on Black Swan, arranged by Grant Still.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: I think about seventy-five cents...sixty-five or seventy-five cents, then they got up to eighty-five and up to a dollar, I think, and I was going to tell you about Mamie Smith. Her name was Mamie...it's been so long...but we travelled with her, I told you, with Bill Bailey's Troubadours. She was the singer--the main singer--with them. Then, her name was Mamie Smart. And then after that broke up, and she went to...to New York, and I think she married a man named Smith. And then she come out with that record--Mamie Smith's 'Crazy Blues,' and then after that, they all commenced. Bessie Smith and her sister, and Ethel Waters, and Alberta Hunter was the first one to sing our song, 'Someday Sweetheart.' Yeah, on the Black Swan Records. That was the first Negro record made--I mean,
company. That was made with Fletcher Henderson and them. All them was in partners then in New York in 1922.

Jazz Oral History Project
Interview with Benjamin "Reb" Spikes
Conducted by Patricia Willard
Cassette 2
When the other tape ran out, you were talking about Black Swan Records, and then you were about to talk about something you did.
Well, Black Swan Records then Alberta Hunter was on it, and she made the first recording of "Someday Sweetheart," and you know Still? The composer and writer? [William] Grant Still?

Well, Grant arranged it, see, and Alberta made it, and it was for the Black Swan Records, and they were owned by Pace...Pace and...I think Pace and Handy, if I'm not mistaken-- Handy's brother, and Fletcher Henderson was the music...was head of the music department.
